scenarios.topic: Saved driver names and future requests
scenarios.title: Repair the names used to request a driver
scenarios.summary: Repair two saved request names while preserving the audit provider and physical settings.
scenarios.objective: Bring the supplied teaching sensor controller online with its existing physical-module settings. Make both saved requests, modprobe capture_current and modprobe capture_legacy, activate that controller’s driver when it is not already loaded. A successful command selecting another provider is insufficient. Preserve the audit provider, all supplied physical-module options and the unrelated audit_query binding. Leave no additional unrequested aliases. Save or revert the editor draft before checking; verify current state and both future requests.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Read which current-state or named-request check failed. A request may return success for the wrong provider; inspect its saved binding and actual driver, repair that state and retry.
steps: Investigate and repair the name bindings

guide.title: Separate a request name from a loaded module
guide.why: An application can request a convenient name instead of a module’s physical name. In the supplied modprobe.d file, alias demo_capture example_reader maps that request to the example_reader module. The alias is a saved lookup rule, not another loaded module: lsmod still shows example_reader. This exercise supports exact names only, not wildcard patterns or alias chains.
guide.action: Insert lspci -k, modprobe demo_capture and lspci -k in that order, then Run each.

commands.explanation: A possible driver is not necessarily active.
Expected command success: this wrong binding selects the already loaded audit provider.
The reader is still unavailable despite status0.

guide.title: Do not confuse a successful command with the right driver
guide.why: The starting demo_capture name points at example_audit, which is already loaded. modprobe demo_capture can therefore succeed without activating the reader. Use lspci -k to inspect the actual driver. In the editor, keep options and the unrelated demo_audit binding, and repair the two requested names. Alias lines are file contents, not terminal commands; Fill practice editor does not save or run them.
guide.action: Select Edit and save the practice name bindings, choose Fill practice editor, read the four lines and click Save configuration. Run modprobe demo_capture and lsmod.

commands.command:
options example_reader queues=1
alias demo_capture example_reader
alias demo_compat example_reader
alias demo_audit example_audit
commands.explanation: File contents for the native editor; choose Save configuration afterward.
Resolve the saved alias and load the physical driver with its dependencies.
The listing contains example_reader, not the alias name.

guide.title: Verify both callers from a clean insertion
guide.why: Save configuration, then request demo_capture and inspect lsmod. Remove only example_reader before requesting demo_compat; modprobe -r preserves dependencies used by the audit provider. Check example tests each declared name with the target unloaded in its own simulated copy. Your live modules do not change during a check. Both future requests and the current controller must work.
guide.action: Run modprobe -r example_reader, then modprobe demo_compat and lspci -k. Choose Check example. Change only demo_capture back to example_audit in the editor, save and check again; restore its worked binding to retry.

commands.explanation: Keep example_audit and any prerequisites it still uses.
Resolve this second saved name from an unloaded reader.
The controller now has its expected driver in use.

In the supplied modprobe.d file, alias demo_capture example_reader maps that request to the example_reader module. The alias is a saved lookup rule, not another loaded module: lsmod still shows example_reader. This exercise supports exact names only, not wildcard patterns or alias chains. In the editor, keep options and the unrelated demo_audit binding, and repair the two requested names. Alias lines are file contents, not terminal commands; Fill practice editor does not save or run them. Save configuration, then request demo_capture and inspect lsmod. Remove only example_reader before requesting demo_compat; modprobe -r preserves dependencies used by the audit provider. Check example tests each declared name with the target unloaded in its own simulated copy. Your live modules do not change during a check. Both future requests and the current controller must work.
hints: Inspect lspci -k and the saved file. A request name and a physical module name have different roles; lsmod shows physical names.
A load request can succeed for an already loaded audit provider. Each requested name must select the controller driver when that driver starts unloaded.
Edit the alias lines for the two requested names. Preserve the physical options and unrelated audit binding; save, activate the controller and check the two future cases.
scenarios.simplifications: Opt-in exact aliases in one virtual modprobe.d file only. No globs, alias chains, ambiguous duplicates, physical-name collisions, alias-specific options, removal by alias, blacklist, script directives, real hardware/kernel/ELF or host execution. Names normalize hyphen and underscore. Each future request is evaluated on a separate bounded in-process copy; grading does not change live modules. This is narrow partial LPIC-2 practice, not full kmod or exam coverage.
